According to the latest issue of the Power On newsletter, Apple reportedly once considered adding a feature to its "Apple Upgrade" programme that would make the process of switching to a new iPhone virtually seamless: transferring users' data before the new device even ships. However, the feature ultimately never came to fruition.

The concept is simple: since users are upgrading through a standard monthly instalment plan, why not make the handover as convenient as possible? Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman reported as follows:

There are some obvious loopholes here. First of all, your iCloud backup would be slightly out of date, since the data can only be transferred at the moment of shipment, which is already several days after the order is placed — unless you pick up the device in person at the store.

Beyond that, there are also obvious privacy concerns. That said, if you've been using iCloud backup all along, it's no surprise that Apple has your data. But typical users might worry about how that data gets transferred to the new phone, and whether anyone has accessed it in the process.

Two years ago, Apple rolled out a brand-new system across all its retail stores called "Presto" that lets staff update software while the iPhone is still in the box. It's hard to imagine this system could one day be expanded to support iCloud backup transfers without anyone ever touching your data.

However, the feature ultimately never made it to market — and that might actually be a good thing.
